facts.statement: Morrosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian age of the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Maastrichtian~

facts.statement: Morrosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur that lived in Antarctica during the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Morrosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous elasmarian dinosaur that lived in the late Cretaceous in Antarctica.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of a euornithopod was discovered in Antarctica in 2002 by paleontologist Fernando Novas.
facts.quote: In 2002, the Argentine paleontologist Fernando Novas reported the discovery of a partial skeleton of a euornithopod in Antarctica.

facts.statement: The species Morrosaurus antarcticus was named and described in 2016 by a team including Sebastian Rozadilla and Fernando Novas.
facts.quote: In 2016 these remains were the basis for naming the type species Morrosaurus antarcticus, named and described by Sebastian Rozadilla, Federico Lisandro Agnolin, Fernando Emilio Novas, Alexis Rolando Aranciaga Mauro, Matthew J. Motta, Juan Manuel Lirio Marcelo, and Pablo Isasi.

facts.statement: The genus name Morrosaurus refers to the fossil site of El Morro on James Ross Island.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the site of El Morro on James Ross Island, where the remains of the species were found.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MACN Pv 197 was found in the Snow Hill Island Formation at Cape Lambe and dates to the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen MACN Pv 197, was found in a layer of the Snow Hill Island Formation (Cape Lambe, previously assigned to the López de Bertodano Formation), dating to the Maastrichtian age.

facts.statement: The known remains consist of a right hind leg, including parts of the femur, tibia, foot, and the first joint of the third toe.
facts.quote: The remains consists in a right hind leg, including the top of the femur, the lower end of the femur, the upper part of the tibia, the underside of the tibia, the upper half of the foot, the bottom of the midfoot and the top of the first joint of the third toe.

facts.statement: The single known specimen is estimated to be between 4.5 and 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: The only known specimen, thought to represent an adult, is estimated to have belong to an individual 4.5-5 m in length.

facts.statement: Morrosaurus was larger and more robust than its relative Trinisaura, which measured only 1.5 meters.
facts.quote: This makes it larger and more robust in skeletal build than many of its relatives, including the fellow Antarctic genus Trinisaura, only 1.5 m in length.

facts.statement: The greater trochanter of Morrosaurus forms an S-shape in bottom view, a trait seen in other elasmarians but more extreme in this species.
facts.quote: In bottom view, the greater trochanter near the top of the femur forms an S-shape, with the back edge thick across and the front edge thin, similar to the condition seen in other elasmarians Anabisetia, Notohypsilophodon, and Gasparinisaura but displayed to a more extreme extent.

facts.statement: Morrosaurus is classified within Iguanodontia as a basal member of Euiguanodontia.
facts.quote: Morrosaurus was classified in the group Iguanodontia, as a basal member of Euiguanodontia.

facts.statement: Morrosaurus belongs to the clade Elasmaria, which includes ornithopods from Patagonia and Antarctica such as Trinisaura and Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: This in turn formed a clade with other ornithopods of Patagonia and Antarctica, particularly Trinisaura, Gasparinisaura, Anabisetia, Notohypsilophodon, Talenkauen and Macrogryphosaurus in a group called Elasmaria

facts.statement: Members of the Elasmaria group, including Morrosaurus, show adaptations for a high-speed running lifestyle indicated by a narrow foot with a thin fourth metatarsal.
facts.quote: whose members are distinguished by their adaptation to a running lifestyle which would be reflected by the narrow foot with a thin fourth metatarsal which indicates a high speed running

facts.statement: The interrupted rapid growth strategy of Morrosaurus was likely an adaptation to the varying resource availability in Antarctica.
facts.quote: This strategy of rapid growith but interruptions would have been a beneficial adaptation in the Antarctic region where resource availability varied throughout the year.

facts.statement: The close relationship between Antarctic Morrosaurus and South American elasmarians demonstrates faunal links between these continents.
facts.quote: Recognition of Antarctic taxa such as Morrosaurus and Trinisaura as being closely related to other elasmarians in South American demonstrated links between the dinosaurs on these continents.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Morrosaurus possessed the specific running adaptations of the Elasmaria clade due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil remains.
facts.quote: It cannot be determined, however, if Morrosaurus itself possessed these characteristics due to their limited remains.

facts.statement: Morrosaurus antarcticus is the only known species of the extinct elasmarian ornithopod dinosaur genus Morrosaurus.
facts.quote: Morrosaurus antarcticus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Morrosaurus de dinosaurio ornitópodo elasmariano

facts.statement: It lived during the late Cretaceous period, 70 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in the area of modern Antarctica.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 70 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en el área de la actual Antártida

facts.statement: In 2002, Argentine paleontologist Fernando Novas reported the discovery of a partial euornithopod skeleton in Antarctica.
facts.quote: En 2002 el paleontólogo argentino Fernando Novas informó sobre el descubrimiento de un esqueleto parcial de un euornitópodo en la Antártida

facts.statement: The species was named and described in 2015 by Sebastián Rozadilla, Federico Lisandro Agnolin, Fernando Emilio Novas, Alexis Mauro Aranciaga Rolando, Matías J. Motta, Juan Manuel Lirio, and Marcelo Pablo Isasi.
facts.quote: En 2015 estos restos fueron la base para denominar a la especie tipo Morrosaurus antarcticus, nombrada y descrita por Sebastián Rozadilla, Federico Lisandro Agnolin, Fernando Emilio Novas, Alexis Mauro Aranciaga Rolando, Matías J. Motta, Juan Manuel Lirio y Marcelo Pablo Isasi

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the El Morro site on James Ross Island where the remains were found.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere al sitio El Morro en la isla James Ross, en donde se encontraron los restos de la especie

facts.statement: The species name refers to Antarctica.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a la Antártida

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MACN Pv 197 was found in a layer of the Snow Hill Island Formation at Cabo Lambe, deposited in the López de Bertodano Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo MACN Pv 197, fue encontrado en una capa de la Formación Snow Hill Island, Cabo Lambe, depositada en la formación López de Bertodano

facts.statement: The type specimen corresponds to a medium-sized animal.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo corresponde a un animal de tamaño mediano

facts.statement: Two unique derived traits were identified: the inferior view of the greater femoral trochanter has a wavy profile with a thick exit edge and a thin main edge.
facts.quote: Dos de estas son autapomorfias, es decir rasgos derivados que son únicos. En vista inferior, el trocánter mayor de fémur tiene un perfil ondulado con un borde de salida grueso y un borde delgado principal

facts.statement: The fourth metatarsal bone has a triangular profile with a backward-pointing projection that wraps around it and the third metatarsal.
facts.quote: El cuarto hueso metatarsiano tiene un perfil triangular con una proyección dirigida hacia atrás que se envuelve alrededor de ella y el tercer metatarsiano

facts.statement: On the femur, the lesser trochanter is inclined diagonally, right next to the greater trochanter.
facts.quote: En el fémur, el trocánter menor se inclina diagonalmente, justo al lado del trocánter mayor

facts.statement: On the tibia, the medial malleolus has a triangular outline and shows a concave anterior surface.
facts.quote: En la tibia, el maleólo en vista medial tiene un contorno triangular y muestra una superficie anterior cóncava

facts.statement: Morrosaurus was placed in the group Iguanodontia as a basal member of Euiguanodontia.
facts.quote: Morrosaurus fue situado en el grupo Iguanodontia, como un miembro basal de Euiguanodontia

facts.statement: It forms a clade with other Patagonian and Antarctic ornithopods, particularly Trinisaura, Gasparinisaura, Anabisetia, Notohypsilophodon, Talenkauen, and Macrogryphosaurus, in a grouping called Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Este forma a su vez un clado con otros ornitópodos de la Patagonia y la Antártida, particularmente Trinisaura, Gasparinisaura, Anabisetia, Notohypsilophodon, Talenkauen y Macrogryphosaurus, en una agrupación denominada Elasmaria

facts.statement: Members of this group are distinguished by an adaptation to a running lifestyle, reflected by a narrow foot with a thin fourth metatarsal indicating high running speed.
facts.quote: cuyos miembros se distinguen por su adaptación a un estilo de vida corredor el cual se vería reflejado por el estrecho pie con un delgado cuarto metatarso el cual indica una alta velocidad al correr

facts.statement: Laterally expanded chevrons are associated with a larger surface for anchoring lateral tail muscles, providing good control of tail movements.
facts.quote: los cheurones expandidos posteriormente, característica que se asocia a una mayor superficie para el anclaje de la musculatura lateral de la cola, lo que le daría un buen control de los movimientos de esta

facts.statement: A curved humerus demonstrates the absence of a deltopectoral crest, meaning the front limb was not used for walking.
facts.quote: un húmero curvado el cual demuestra la ausencia de una cresta deltopectoral y que por tanto la pata delantera no era usada para caminar

facts.statement: It cannot be determined whether Morrosaurus itself possessed these characteristics due to its limited remains.
facts.quote: No se puede determinar, sin embargo, si el propio Morrosaurus poseía estas características debido a sus restos limitados

facts.statement: The time range is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
